A. have and have got

A. have và have got

I have (something) or I’ve got (something) = it is mine:

I have (something) hoặc I’ve got (something) = nó là của tôi, tôi có:

  • I have a new car. or I’ve got a new car.

    Tôi có xe mới.

  • Sue has long hair. or Sue has got long hair.

    Sue để tóc dài.

  • Do they have any children? or Have they got any children?

    Họ có con không?

  • Tom doesn’t have a job. or Tom hasn’t got a job.

    Tom không có việc làm.

  • How much time do you have? or How much time have you got?

    Bạn có bao nhiêu thời gian?

also I have / I’ve got a headache / (a) toothache / a pain (in my leg etc.) / a cold / a cough / a sore throat / a temperature / flu etc.

ngoài ra I have / I’ve got a headache (đau đầu) / (a) toothache (đau răng) / a pain (đau ở chân v.v.) / a cold (cảm lạnh) / a cough (ho) / a sore throat (đau họng) / a temperature (sốt) / flu (cúm) v.v.

  • I have a headache. or I’ve got a headache.

    Tôi bị đau đầu.

  • Do you have a cold? or Have you got a cold?

    Bạn bị cảm à?

The past is I had (without got) / I didn’t have / Did you have? etc.:

Quá khứ là I had (không có got) / I didn’t have / Did you have? v.v.:

  • When I first met Sue, she had short hair.

    Lần đầu tôi gặp Sue, cô ấy để tóc ngắn.

  • He didn’t have any money because he didn’t have a job.

    Anh ấy không có tiền vì không có việc làm.

  • Did you have enough time to do everything you wanted?

    Bạn có đủ thời gian làm mọi việc mình muốn không?

B. have breakfast / have a shower etc.

B. have breakfast / have a shower v.v.

In these expressions have = eat / drink / take etc. You can’t use ‘have got’.

Trong các cụm này have = ăn / uống / dùng v.v. Không thể dùng ‘have got’.

have breakfast / lunch / dinner; a meal / a sandwich / a pizza etc.; a cup of coffee / a glass of milk etc.; something to eat/drink

have breakfast / lunch / dinner (ăn sáng / trưa / tối); a meal / a sandwich / a pizza (ăn …); a cup of coffee / a glass of milk (uống …); something to eat/drink (ăn/uống gì đó)

  • ‘Where’s Lisa?’ ‘She’s having lunch.’

    ‘Lisa đâu?’ ‘Cô ấy đang ăn trưa.’

  • I don’t usually have breakfast.

    Tôi thường không ăn sáng.

  • I had three cups of coffee this morning.

    Sáng nay tôi uống ba tách cà phê.

  • ‘Have a biscuit!’ ‘Oh, thank you.’

    ‘Ăn bánh quy đi!’ ‘Ồ, cảm ơn.’

We also use have (not have got) in these expressions: have a bath / a shower; a rest / a holiday / a party; a nice time / a good trip / fun etc.; a walk / a swim / a game (of tennis etc.); a dream / an accident; a baby; a look (at something)

Cũng dùng have (không dùng have got) trong các cụm: have a bath / a shower (tắm); a rest / a holiday / a party (nghỉ ngơi / đi nghỉ / tổ chức tiệc); a nice time / a good trip / fun (vui vẻ); a walk / a swim / a game (đi dạo / bơi / chơi một ván); a dream / an accident (mơ / gặp tai nạn); a baby (sinh con); a look (nhìn qua)

  • I had a shower this morning.

    Sáng nay tôi đã tắm.

  • We’re having a party next week. You must come.

    Tuần sau chúng tôi tổ chức tiệc. Bạn phải đến nhé.

  • Enjoy your holiday. Have a nice time!

    Đi nghỉ vui nhé. Chúc vui vẻ!

  • Did you have a good time in Tokyo?

    Ở Tokyo bạn có vui không?

  • Sandra has just had a baby.

    Sandra vừa sinh em bé.

  • Can I have a look at your magazine?

    Tôi xem qua tạp chí của bạn được không?

C. have or have got / have (not have got)

C. have hoặc have got / have (không dùng have got)

  • I have / I’ve got a new shower. It’s very good. (= it is mine)

    Tôi có vòi sen mới. Nó rất tốt.

  • I have a shower every morning. (not I’ve got a shower every morning)

    Sáng nào tôi cũng tắm vòi sen. (không nói I’ve got a shower every morning)

  • A: Where’s Paul? B: He’s having a shower. (= he’s washing now)

    A: Paul đâu? B: Anh ấy đang tắm.

have / have got = sở hữu (và bệnh: a headache, a cold …).
